CV choice: Linear regression

?How the default model was chosen

Linear regression was selected using 5-fold cross-validation on the
training rows. 15 settings were tried; one fitted representative per
successful family is kept here.[Inspect the search](#selection)Score
definitions

?Score definitions

RMSE: Typical prediction error, with larger mistakes weighted more
heavily; lower is better. MAE: Average absolute prediction error in the
target's units; lower is better. R-squared: Share of evaluation-set
variation explained relative to predicting the evaluation-set mean;
higher is better.

### Performance vs cost ?Reading the cost chartLeft means lower measured cost. For a loss such as RMSE or log loss, lower is better; for accuracy or R-squared, higher is better. Outlined models are not beaten on both axes. Single-fit millisecond timings are descriptive readings, not reliable speed rankings. R object size includes retained diagnostics, may count shared data repeatedly and excludes native engine allocations. It is not a saved-file or deployment-memory comparison.

Compare cost Model size (KiB) Training time (ms) Prediction time (ms)

Cost scale Linear Log

?Choosing a cost scale

Linear spacing compares absolute cost differences. Log spacing compares
ratios: 1 to 10 uses the same space as 10 to 100. It can separate
inexpensive models when one model is much larger or slower. All plotted
costs must be positive; scores and the Pareto frontier do not change.

Score scale Linear Log

?Choosing a score scale

Log spacing compares ratios between positive losses. It can separate
useful models when one alternative has a much larger error. All models
and their original scores remain visible. Zero losses and scores such as
accuracy or R-squared use a linear axis.

Linear cost axis. Scale switching requires JavaScript.

Reading the chart

The lower left combines a better score with less resource use. Outlined
points form the observed Pareto frontier: no other displayed model is at
least as good on both axes and strictly better on one. Dashed steps show
the best observed score available within each resource budget, between
the first and last frontier measurements. The corners between points are
budget boundaries, not fitted models or interpolated scores. Thin
colored lines connect names to points. This comparison does not account
for measurement uncertainty and does not select a model. Nearly equal
measurements share a display range of at least 0.1% of their magnitude;
exact values and frontier membership are unchanged.

How costs were measured

Times are measured on this machine. Fit time covers the retained fit,
not the entire cross-validation search; prediction time covers this
evaluation batch. A displayed ~0 means no elapsed time was recorded;
timer resolution varies by platform. It does not mean the operation
takes no time. Size estimates the retained R model object. R object size
includes retained diagnostics, may count shared data repeatedly and
excludes native engine allocations. It is not a saved-file or
deployment-memory comparison, or a count of learned rules. These
measurements are not hardware-independent benchmarks.

Measure repeated prediction costs

A single timer reading can be too coarse for small models. Measure
repeated predictions on a common batch to compare their costs.

```
bench <- benchmark_predictions(result)
render_model_report(result, "report.html", benchmark = bench)
```

### Neural network: search rationale

Small single-layer networks and several weight penalties bound the
search cost. Numeric inputs and regression outcomes are standardized
using each training fold. The default 2,000-iteration cap gives
difficult fits more time; converged fits stop early. Changing only maxit
preserves initialization, and nonconverged fits remain excluded by
default. 7 of 12 available tuples scheduled; 5 untested.

Preset values are package choices, not data-optimized ranges.

**Tested:** size: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 · decay: 0.1, 0.001, 0.03, 0.01 · maxit:
2000

Family CV winner is at a tested edge: size = 1; decay = 0.1. Other
controls may vary too; extending one range is a new experiment, not an
expected improvement.

### Decision tree: search rationale

Preset tuples move from shallow trees and larger minimum splits toward
deeper trees. Minimum split sizes are fractions of outer-training row
count, bounded below by four. 7 of 12 available tuples scheduled; 5
untested.

Preset values are package choices, not data-optimized ranges.

**Tested:** maxdepth: 10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 · cp: 0.0005, 0.001, 0.003,
0.01, 0.03 · minsplit: 14, 23, 35, 58

Family CV winner is at a tested edge: maxdepth = 10; cp = 5e-04;
minsplit = 14. Other controls may vary too; extending one range is a new
experiment, not an expected improvement.

Exact selection arithmetic and preference order

Eligible loss ≤ 2.934817 + 0.160368 = **3.095186**. Among eligible
candidates: first the preferred family, then its smallest recorded
capacity proxy, then score and configuration ID to break a tie.

| Family            | Preference order | Within-family capacity proxy       |
|-------------------|------------------|------------------------------------|
| Linear regression | 1                | potential coefficient count        |
| Decision tree     | 4                | within-family potential leaf count |
| Neural network    | 9                | within-family connection count     |

Values: Family, Preference order, Within-family capacity proxy

Family order is package or user preference. Capacity proxies omit some
regularization controls; they do not establish a universal
least-flexible model.

RMSE is the square root of squared losses pooled across validation rows.
Fold-score SE is a selection heuristic. Training folds overlap; it is
not a confidence interval, equivalence test or population uncertainty.

Preprocessing was learned again inside every fold. The evaluation
partition was not used to choose hyperparameters. Full fold assignments
and any retained out-of-fold predictions remain in
`tuning_results(result)`.

Why this grid? Coverage, parameter meaning and boundary winners

Round-robin ordered grid prefixes; explicit family budgets override the
total allocation. Outer training rows: 288; raw inputs: 5.

Exact preset numbers are package engineering choices, not values
justified as optimal by literature. This finite joint-configuration
search does not identify causal effects of individual settings.

| Family | Grid source | Available tuples | Scheduled tuples | Untested tuples | Rationale |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| linear | package_presets | 1 | 1 | 0 | One unpenalized reference fit; there is no parameter grid for this family. |
| tree | package_presets | 12 | 7 | 5 | Preset tuples move from shallow trees and larger minimum splits toward deeper trees. Minimum split sizes are fractions of outer-training row count, bounded below by four. |
| neural | package_presets | 12 | 7 | 5 | Small single-layer networks and several weight penalties bound the search cost. Numeric inputs and regression outcomes are standardized using each training fold. The default 2,000-iteration cap gives difficult fits more time; converged fits stop early. Changing only maxit preserves initialization, and nonconverged fits remain excluded by default. |

Recorded search budget and rationale

| Family | Parameter | Available preset values | Meaning |
|----|----|----|----|
| tree | maxdepth | 2, 4, 6, 10, 3, 5, 8 | Maximum permitted tree depth, not observed depth. |
| tree | cp | 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, 0.0005, 0.001, 0 | Larger thresholds discourage small-improvement splits. |
| tree | minsplit | 58, 35, 23, 14, 9, 6 | Minimum training rows in a node before attempting a split. |
| neural | size | 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 | Hidden units in one layer; more units permit more patterns. |
| neural | decay | 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001, 0, 0.0001 | Weight penalty; larger values discourage large weights. |
| neural | maxit | 2000 | Optimizer iteration limit. It can stop earlier; a larger limit does not guarantee convergence. |

| family | configuration_id | parameter | selected_value | tested_min | tested_max | distinct_values | position |

| neural | neural_01 | size | 1.00 | 1.00 | 8.00 | 5 | lower edge |
| neural | neural_01 | decay | 0.10 | 0.001 | 0.10 | 4 | upper edge |
| neural | neural_01 | maxit | 2000.00 | 2000.00 | 2000.00 | 1 | fixed |

| tree | tree_04 | cp | 5e-04 | 5e-04 | 0.03 | 5 | lower edge |
| tree | tree_04 | minsplit | 14.00 | 14.00 | 58.00 | 4 | lower edge |

Position of each family CV winner within scheduled numeric settings

A fixed setting was not varied. An edge winner can motivate a new
training-only comparison; it does not show that extending one control
would help, because several controls may differ between the tested
tuples.

Refit attempts; evaluation scores do not choose a fallback

Copy and change this search grid in R

This executable control reproduces the scheduled tuples and budgets.
Edit a tuple to test a specific hypothesis. Refit using your original
data, preprocessing, validation design and seed. This control alone does
not reproduce the entire analysis. Avoid repeatedly tuning against the
evaluation partition.

    control <- tuning_control(
      grids = list(linear = list(list()), tree = list(list(maxdepth = 2L, cp = 0.03,
        minsplit = 58L), list(maxdepth = 4L, cp = 0.01, minsplit = 35L),
        list(maxdepth = 6L, cp = 0.003, minsplit = 23L), list(maxdepth = 10L,
            cp = 5e-04, minsplit = 14L), list(maxdepth = 3L, cp = 0.01,
            minsplit = 58L), list(maxdepth = 5L, cp = 0.003, minsplit = 23L),
        list(maxdepth = 8L, cp = 0.001, minsplit = 14L)), neural = list(
        list(size = 1L, decay = 0.1, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 2L,
            decay = 0.03, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 4L, decay = 0.01,
            maxit = 2000L), list(size = 6L, decay = 0.01, maxit = 2000L),
        list(size = 8L, decay = 0.001, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 2L,
            decay = 0.001, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 4L, decay = 0.001,
            maxit = 2000L))),
      family_budgets = c(linear = 1L, tree = 7L, neural = 7L),
      metric = "rmse",
      optimization_policy = "exclude",
      family_priority = c("linear", "tree", "neural")
    )
    # In your original autoxplain(...) call, use:
    #   learners = c("linear", "tree", "neural"), max_models = NULL, tuning_control = control
    #   tuning_rule = "one_se", seed = 2026
    # Keep the original preprocessing and validation design (including supplied fold IDs).

Use `tuning_evidence(result)` for the aggregate record.

Method references and limits

These sources explain selection bias, fold variability and backend
controls. They do not validate this package’s exact preset numbers or
family preference order.

What this file contains

This HTML includes 360 individual records across 6 columns, including
rows hidden by filters. Aggregate output is not anonymization. Anyone
receiving row-mode HTML receives every embedded record.

Columns: delivery_hours, distance_km, parcel_kg, dispatch_backlog,
service, planned_route_hours

Raw supplied rows and processed retained rows are distinct populations.

Proportional split allocation; uniform sample without replacement within
each split; seed 2026

Individual-column summaries use all available rows. Relationship counts,
conditional summaries and associations describe the analyzed sample.
Individual-column summaries use all rows. Rare groups may be missed by
sampling. Pair summaries: 15 of 15. Target pairs first, then original
column order; all individual profiles are retained

## Feature importance & effects?Exploring fitted effectsALE follows local changes in predictions and centers the effect at zero. Negative effects mean below this reference, not negative probabilities. PDP averages predictions with an input set to each displayed value. A flat average curve can hide interactions, even for an important feature. These describe fitted associations, not the consequences of an intervention.

## Checks requiring attention

### Near-optimal models disagree on the feature-importance ranking.

Mean Spearman agreement: 0.7

**Next:** [Compare feature-importance ranges across the supplied
candidates.](#candidate-importance-ranges)

Diagnostic coverage and association evidence

**evaluation: computed.** Ordered observations, outcomes and event
semantics agree; independence and representativeness are not established
by these checks.

**association: computed.** Limited pairwise screen: absolute Spearman
correlation for numeric pairs, correlation ratio for mixed pairs, and
Cramer's V for categorical pairs. Small values do not establish
independence or exclude nonlinear or joint dependence. Categorical pairs
without repeated categories are unavailable; many rare categories can
inflate association.

**permutation: computed.** Loss changes describe these shuffles. The
intervals quantify shuffle randomness, not sampling, fitting or
selection uncertainty.

**comparison: computed.** Observed candidate disagreement does not bound
all models or establish a unique explanation.

**resources: computed.**

**model_behavior: computed.**

**prediction_disagreement: computed.**

**decision_cutoffs: not applicable.** Decision-cutoff comparisons apply
to binary classification.

Feature association screen

Limited pairwise screen: absolute Spearman correlation for numeric
pairs, correlation ratio for mixed pairs, and Cramer's V for categorical
pairs. Small values do not establish independence or exclude nonlinear
or joint dependence. Categorical pairs without repeated categories are
unavailable; many rare categories can inflate association.

Interval method and assumptions

Paired percentile intervals conditional on the fitted models, from 1000
bootstrap draws. These intervals omit fitting and selection uncertainty
and assume independent sampling units.

Run settings and validation design

- Target: delivery_hours
- Task: regression
- Engine: base
- Training rows: 288
- Evaluation rows: 72
- Evaluation role: test
- Split: reproducible random holdout
- Selection: Selected using 5 training folds; evaluation rows did not
  select this model.
- Seed: 2026
- Package version: 0.7.0

Metric definitions

Definitions for every metric

- RMSE: Typical prediction error, with larger mistakes weighted more
  heavily; lower is better.
- MAE: Average absolute prediction error in the target's units; lower is
  better.
- R-squared: Share of evaluation-set variation explained relative to
  predicting the evaluation-set mean; higher is better.
